stories.h: The Caribbean is finally building a ferry service between its own islands
stories.w: CARICOM set a September deadline for the regulatory framework and Trinidad has offered a vessel for the pilot. Moving between neighbouring islands has long meant flying, often via Miami.

stories.h: CARICOM is fighting over who runs it, and one member wants a court to decide
stories.w: Trinidad and Tobago wants the Caribbean Court of Justice to rule on the secretary general's reappointment. Jamaica is not contesting it. The tenure ends in late August regardless.

stories.h: Mexico stripped officials of the right to decide what they keep secret
stories.w: Sheinbaum's 4 August decree widens disclosure across contracts, audits and the Pemex and CFE subsidiaries. The bigger package goes to Congress in September.

stories.h: Brazil auctioned oil blocks at the mouth of the Amazon months before hosting COP30
stories.w: Chevron, ExxonMobil, Petrobras and China's CNPC took blocks in the Foz do Amazonas basin. Indigenous and environmental groups are fighting it; the climate summit is in Belém.

stories.h: Argentina's Supreme Court told the president there are things only Congress can do
stories.w: On 14 August the court struck down part of an emergency decree. Milei has governed heavily by decree, and this is the first hard limit from a body he cannot dissolve.

stories.h: Argentina can now expel foreigners for speech the government calls hateful
stories.w: Decree 681/2026 covers barring entry and removing people already there. Who decides what counts as vilifying Argentines is the question nobody has answered.

stories.h: France banned cold calling outright, with fines up to €375,000 per call
stories.w: From 11 August, telemarketers need your consent first — an opt-in, not an opt-out. Individuals face up to €75,000 per call, companies five times that.

stories.h: France became the first EU country to bar under-15s from social media
stories.w: Australia went first globally; France is the first inside the bloc, which means 26 other governments now have a working precedent and a legal fight to watch.

stories.h: From 2 August, AI in the EU has to say it is AI
stories.w: Deepfakes need labels and chatbots need to disclose themselves, across all 27 members at once. The rules apply directly — no national parliament had to pass anything.

stories.h: The EU wants to tax vapes and nicotine pouches for the first time
stories.w: It is the biggest rewrite of tobacco taxation in a decade, and it needs every member state to agree. Parliament already failed to take a position in June.

stories.h: Around 60,000 people crossed into Ceuta from Morocco in days
stories.w: Social media rumours and economic pressure drove the surge into Spain's North African enclave. Ceuta has about 85,000 residents.

stories.h: 289 Kenyans were recruited into Russia's military. At least 69 are dead or missing.
stories.w: Families are still trying to find out what happened to them. Kenya's own government put out the number, which is what makes it official rather than rumour.

stories.h: Burkina Faso dissolved 118 organisations and suspended 564 more
stories.w: Civicus added the country to its human rights watchlist over the scale of it. That is most of the country's organised civil society, gone by administrative order.

stories.h: Ghana's government backed five-year terms and a presidential age floor of 35
stories.w: The government accepted proposals for five-year presidential and parliamentary terms and wants the minimum presidential age cut from 40 to 35. The constitution has not changed yet; this is the government's position.

stories.h: The world's two biggest cocoa producers signed a pact to stop undercutting each other
stories.w: Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire grow most of the world's cocoa and have historically competed on price, which meant farmers absorbed the losses. Acting together is the whole point.

stories.h: Kenya passed a law setting out how citizens must be consulted before government decisions
stories.w: The Public Participation Bill applies to national and county government, parliament, the judiciary and state corporations. Consultation stops being a favour and becomes a procedure.

stories.h: A Sudanese army drone struck a traditional village court in North Darfur, killing 35
stories.w: The court was in territory held by the RSF. Two years into this war, the places people go to settle ordinary disputes are now targets.

stories.h: Macky Sall's run at the UN's top job collapsed in a straw poll
stories.w: Senegal's former president had assumed African backing would carry him. The poll showed it isn't there, and the campaign is effectively finished before it started.

stories.h: Mali's former prime minister walked out of prison after serving a sentence for criticising the junta
stories.w: Moussa Mara was jailed for what he said about the military government. He announced his own release, which tells you something about how the news gets out now.

stories.h: South Africa switched on digital travel authorisation with biometric checks before arrival
stories.w: Visitor visas and stay extensions move online under the Immigration Act. The queue at Home Affairs was the single most complained-about experience in the country.

stories.h: Nigeria sent 86 troops to hold up a neighbour's transition
stories.w: The ECOWAS stabilisation mission in Guinea-Bissau is West Africa policing West Africa. After a run of coups, the bloc is testing whether it still can.

stories.h: Indonesia's bullet train lost 5.1 trillion rupiah in six months
stories.w: Whoosh was the flagship of the country's infrastructure push and the losses land on state-owned firms. Every country weighing a high-speed line is reading the balance sheet.

stories.h: South Korea's Supreme Court confirmed Nippon Steel owes compensation for wartime forced labour
stories.w: The ruling covers relatives of a man held at the Kamaishi works. It landed on Liberation Day week, when the president was calling for closer ties with Japan.

stories.h: Malaysia wants to tax electric vehicles to pay for the chargers they need
stories.w: EV owners currently pay nothing toward the public network everyone else's EVs will also need. Charging it to the cars is a bet that the fleet is now big enough to fund itself.

stories.h: The Philippines' new AI push comes with a bill in power, water and land
stories.w: Pax Silica needs all three in a country that is short of the first two. The trade-off is being argued about before the data centres are built, which is unusual.

stories.h: Vietnam is rewriting the rules for how religious organisations operate
stories.w: The legal framework governing registration and activity is being modernised wholesale. In a one-party state, the terms on which faith groups exist are set by statute.

stories.h: Indonesia fired 137 people from its free school meals programme
stories.w: The scheme is the president's signature promise and it is being restructured mid-flight. Feeding tens of millions of children turns out to be an operations problem, not a budget one.

stories.h: Cambodia is racing a clock most countries don't know they have
stories.w: The government is building policy around its demographic window — the years when working-age people outnumber dependents — aiming for high-income status by 2050. Miss it and it does not come back.

stories.h: Myanmar's strategic oil pipeline is running dry
stories.w: It was built to give China a route bypassing the Malacca Strait, and it is one of the junta's few reliable earners. Depletion narrows an already short list.

stories.h: Malaysia built a three-tier plan to keep eating if the shipping lanes close
stories.w: The strategy is explicitly designed around disruption in West Asia. Food security stopped being an agriculture question and became a logistics one.

stories.h: Thailand needs far more migrant workers than it is comfortable admitting
stories.w: The workforce doing the country's hardest jobs is largely foreign and largely undiscussed. The economics and the politics are pointing in opposite directions.

stories.h: Vanuatu launched four climate finance initiatives at once
stories.w: A country of roughly 330,000 people is building the machinery to receive and spend climate money on its own terms, rather than through whoever is offering it.

stories.h: Vanuatu and Timor-Leste dropped visas for each other
stories.w: Two small states that rarely appear in each other's news agreed people can just go. Neither needed a larger power to broker it.

stories.h: Fiji backed a united Pacific line against missile testing in the region's waters
stories.w: New Zealand is pushing a joint statement over China's testing. For Pacific states the ocean is not a backdrop to somebody else's strategy — it is the country.

stories.h: Vanuatu turned 46 and spent the day arguing about unity
stories.w: Independence Day drew crowds and a round of speeches about holding the country together. A national birthday used as a political forum is its own kind of healthy.
